title: Recommendations
approach: The predictors of i are the segments containing [l_i, r_i], and their intersection is [max l_j, min r_j] over those j — so the answer is (l_i - maxL) + (minR - r_i). Both extremes come from one sorted sweep each: sort by l ascending, r descending and every earlier segment already satisfies l_j <= l_i, so the smallest r_j >= r_i in a multiset of seen r's is minR; sort by r descending, l ascending and the largest l_j <= l_i in a multiset of seen l's is maxL. Two edge cases print 0: a duplicate segment (it is its own predictor, so the intersection is exactly [l, r]) and a user with no predictor at all.

techniques.label: line-sweep
techniques.why: each answer is computed from the segments already seen in a sorted order — the sweep IS the algorithm

techniques.label: ordered-set
techniques.why: the multiset of seen endpoints, queried with lower_bound/upper_bound

techniques.label: sorting
techniques.why: two different orders, (l asc, r desc) and (r desc, l asc), each making one containment condition automatic

techniques.label: binary-search
techniques.why: lower_bound/upper_bound inside the multiset — plain binary search over a sorted container, NOT binary search on the answer

techniques.label: two-pointers
techniques.why: Codeforces tags a two-pointer variant; the sorted sweep can be walked with pointers instead of a multiset

verified: not independently verified — the approach is the solution the maintainer supplied, read against the statement
